headline: Compromised suppliers drove the day's worst losses, moving $133 million out of Crédit Mutuel Arkéa, warming the cold rooms at three French blood banks, and spilling customer data from six Asian airlines through Amadeus IT Group.

emerging_trends.text: Third-party suppliers delivered the day's largest damage, with Crédit Mutuel Arkéa watching an estimated $133 million leave through a compromised vendor, the Établissement français du sang finding its blood cold rooms warmed through a refrigeration equipment provider, and six Asian airlines tracing stolen passenger records to Amadeus IT Group.

Attackers keep picking the software distribution path, poisoning cPGuard updates on nearly 3,000 hosting servers, swapping verified APT packages on Debian and Ubuntu machines, and firing a zero-day at roughly 1,000 Zyxel GS1900 switches.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Poisoned cPGuard Updates Reach Nearly 3,000 Servers

emerging_trends.text: AI tooling now works both sides of an intrusion: Binance blames compromised internal AI tools for part of its $6.34 billion loss, and WorkOS, Northflank, and Trigger.dev report attackers who harvested customers' AI access tokens and drove ARTEX to automate the break-ins.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Stolen AI Tokens Widen Provider Breaches

topics.title: Binance Report Names a Rigged Coding Assignment
topics.latest_developments: Binance's first full incident report, detailed November 4, 2026, traces the $6.34 billion theft to a rigged coding assignment handed to engineers during fake recruitment interviews and counts three engineers' computers compromised, one more than the exchange described a day earlier, with the attackers also abusing compromised internal AI tooling before reaching the wallet infrastructure; North Korea fired missiles toward the sea the same day while protesting United States claims that it ran the heist.
topics.summary: Suspected North Korean operators spent months working Binance engineers through recruitment-themed social engineering, a tampered Homebrew installation, and endpoint compromise to reach the systems that sign withdrawals. Any company whose engineers download code from strangers during interviews should treat take-home assignments as untrusted and isolate them.

sources.title: Rigged Coding Assignment, Abused AI Tool Opened Path to $6 Billion Binance Heist
Fake job interview opened the door to $6.34 billion Binance heist
Binance says hackers who stole billions in crypto spent months planning heist
North Korea Launches Missiles Toward the Sea as Pyongyang Protests Against US Claims on Binance Hack

topics.title: Refrigeration Attacks Reach French Blood Banks
topics.latest_developments: The Établissement français du sang, the only civilian blood collection and transfusion organization in France, said attackers reached a refrigeration equipment supplier and raised the temperature and defrost settings at three of its sites this week, and its monitoring systems caught the spikes in the cold rooms early enough for staff to reverse them before the blood spoiled.
topics.summary: The same Europe-wide wave that defrosted supermarket cases in Belgium, Sweden, Ireland, Estonia, and the United Kingdom early Monday, November 2, 2026 now reaches medical cold storage, and the French blood service took the hit through a vendor rather than its own network. Operators of temperature-controlled infrastructure should cut remote access to refrigeration controllers, inventory supplier connections into them, and alarm on setpoint changes.

Cyberattack hits French blood banks
Cyberattack disrupts blood storage refrigeration systems in France
Fresh European Fridge Attacks Put Cold-Chain Security in Focus

topics.title: Poisoned cPGuard Updates Reach Nearly 3,000 Servers
topics.latest_developments: OPSShield put the reach of the hijacked update channel at nearly 3,000 customer servers on November 4, 2026, named the poisoned builds as cPGuard versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19, and said the attacker logged into its update servers with compromised credentials and also took customer contact information and hashed passwords off its billing and licensing server.
topics.summary: cPGuard is a security suite OPSShield sells for Linux web hosting servers; the fake updates installed a backdoor and collected password hashes and other sensitive files, some of which the attacker has already exfiltrated. Hosting operators running the affected versions should treat the servers as compromised, rebuild, and rotate every credential stored on them.

sources.title: Poisoned cPGuard update hits thousands of web hosting servers

topics.title: Xen, Rails, Chrome, and Android Ship Critical Fixes
topics.latest_developments: The Xen Project disclosed two flaws on November 3, 2026 that let one malicious guest virtual machine read and write the memory of every other virtual machine on the host, dom0 included, reaching all Xen releases from 4.6 onward with patches out and no mitigation available; the Rails project fixed a critical Active Storage flaw in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2 that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files and read sensitive ones on servers that process uploads through ImageMagick, which Dark Reading said positions an attacker for lateral movement; Google shipped Chrome 157 with 213 security fixes, seven of them critical; and Google gave the Android remote code execution flaw that needs no user interaction the identifier CVE-2026-58868, covering Android 14 through 17.
topics.summary: The Xen bugs break the wall between tenants on a shared host, the Rails bug hands file writes to anyone who can upload an image, and the Android flaw runs code on a phone with no action by its owner. Administrators should apply the Xen patches, move to Rails 8.1.4.1 or 8.0.5.2, take Chrome 157, and require Android security patch level 2026-11-01 or later.

sources.title: Xen Hypervisor Flaws Let One Malicious VM Read and Write Any Other VM's Memory
Critical Rails Bug Threatens to Derail Vulnerable Servers

topics.title: APT Package Verification Falls to a Download Swap
topics.latest_developments: Zyxel patched a zero-day in its GS1900 series network switches that attackers used to compromise nearly 1,000 devices worldwide and steal configuration files and credentials, reported November 4, 2026; Debian, Ubuntu, and the APT developers published advisories the same day for a flaw that lets an attacker who can modify package downloads substitute their own file for a verified package and run code as root, an attack that rides APT's habit of retrying failed downloads, the default from Debian 12 onward; and SonicWall said it will leave two flaws unpatched in Global Management System 9.5.2 and earlier, which it has taken end of life, among them CVE-2026-109593, an unauthenticated file read rated 9.1 that exposes internal GMS files to anyone with network access, alongside a second bug that alters database records.
topics.summary: APT installs and updates software on most Debian and Ubuntu machines, so a machine-in-the-middle on any plain-HTTP mirror turns routine patching into root compromise. Administrators should install the new APT packages, point systems at mirrors reached over HTTPS, update GS1900 switches and rotate their credentials, and move off SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier, which will never receive a fix.

sources.title: Debian and Ubuntu APT Flaw Lets MitM Attackers Swap Verified Packages and Run Code as Root
Zyxel fixes zero-day exploited to hack nearly 1,000 network switches

topics.title: Russian-Linked Watering Holes Hit iOS and Android
topics.latest_developments: Sekoia pinned the campaign on Russia's APT29 on November 4, 2026, said its Threat Detection and Research team spotted the operation in mid-October 2026, traced part of the delivery to a supply chain compromise of Plerdy SEO Tracker, a Ukrainian web analytics service whose hijacked JavaScript fingerprints a visitor's browser and device before the exploits fire and then steals cookies, messages, and Wi-Fi passwords, and told Ars Technica the operators appear to hunt diplomatic targets.
topics.summary: The campaign reuses vulnerabilities Apple and Google have already patched, so a phone that reaches the current security patch level blocks the chain and an outdated one falls with no tap from the owner, whether the visitor loads a compromised site or a lookalike portal. Phone owners should install pending iOS and Android updates immediately.

topics.title: Stolen AI Tokens Widen Provider Breaches
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported on November 4, 2026 that the development platform Trigger.dev joins WorkOS and Northflank among the providers disclosing intrusions in which attackers harvested customers' AI access tokens and drove AI-assisted offensive tooling to automate the break-ins, and mSeven Software told current and former mSecure password manager customers to change passwords, reset two-factor authentication, and remove passkeys after an attack that reportedly exposed an encrypted customer database.
topics.summary: WorkOS blamed ARTEX, the AI penetration-testing framework CrowdStrike attributes to the China-based group Vapor Panda, for the theft of business contact records and customer communication summaries, and Chainstack exposed customer data and password hashes in the same wave. Any company that stores AI API keys on a third-party platform should rotate them now and cap per-key spending.

sources.title: AI-Linked Breaches Mount as WorkOS, Northflank, Trigger.dev Disclose Hacks

topics.title: Amadeus and DreamHost Breaches Reach Downstream Customers
topics.latest_developments: Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Korean Air, Asiana Airlines, Singapore Airlines, and Malaysia Airlines have all reported data breaches over the past week that they trace to Amadeus IT Group, the Spanish company that builds and runs their flight reservation, ticketing, and check-in platforms; DreamHost confirmed on November 4, 2026 that attackers held access to its File Manager platform for two months and took customers' FTP and SFTP usernames and passwords along with webmail sessions.
topics.summary: One compromise at Amadeus put passenger records from six Asian carriers into an attacker's hands, and the DreamHost intrusion hands over working credentials to every site those customers host. DreamHost customers should change FTP and SFTP passwords, invalidate webmail sessions, and audit site files for changes made during the two-month window.

sources.title: More Asian airlines announce data breaches after attack on Spanish IT provider Amadeus
DreamHost confirms data breach exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions

topics.title: Attack Wipes Beget's Cloud Data
topics.latest_developments: The Record reported on November 4, 2026 that Beget, a major Russian web hosting provider, is struggling to restore service after a cyberattack destroyed data across its cloud infrastructure and knocked hundreds of websites offline, and that a suspected Russian cyberattack the same day disrupted the website of The Kyiv Independent, one of Ukraine's leading English-language news outlets.
topics.summary: Destructive attacks on a hosting provider take every tenant down at once and leave customers dependent on backups they hold themselves. Anyone hosting on a shared provider should keep an independent copy of code and data outside that provider.

sources.title: Cyberattack wipes cloud data at major Russian hosting provider Beget

topics.title: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Loses $133 Million
topics.latest_developments: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa, the French cooperative banking group, confirmed in a press notice on November 4, 2026 that attackers compromised one of its suppliers, which the bank left unnamed, and then moved an estimated $133 million by making transfers out of the bank's own account.
topics.summary: The intruders used supplier access to issue payments as the bank itself, which turns a vendor compromise into direct theft of funds. Banks should treat supplier connections into payment systems as privileged, require separate approval for transfers from house accounts, and reconcile those accounts daily.

sources.title: French bank confirms cyber heist, hackers suspected to have stolen an estimated $133 million

business_politics.title: Democrats Sweep Congress
business_politics.latest_developments: Vice President JD Vance broke with President Trump late Wednesday, November 4, blaming the Iran war for the Republican collapse while administration officials argued over whether to escalate strikes; House Speaker Mike Johnson told colleagues he will not seek election as House Republican leader, party figures turned on Trump, his candidates, and his staff over the war, the cost of living, and corruption allegations, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average posted its best day in 18 months as traders bet on legislative gridlock, lifting hyperscalers and knocking chipmakers down. The Financial Times calculated that the technology industry's $600 million midterm campaign bought almost nothing, including Elon Musk's $440 million and the roughly $30 billion of election-related paper losses he absorbed, and The Economist expects the new Democratic majorities to pass few laws and open a torrent of investigations.
business_politics.summary: American voters punished President Trump's party Tuesday, November 3, over the cost of living, with three-quarters of those surveyed calling the economy not so good or poor and those voters backing Democrats overwhelmingly; in Texas, Democrat James Talarico beat Republican Ken Paxton, whose campaign Musk bankrolled with $47 million. Divided government for Trump's final two years hands Democrats subpoena power and sets up fights over Iran, Ukraine, and taxes, and House Democrats are already preparing to haul artificial-intelligence executives in to testify under oath.

business_politics.title: Oil Falls as Trump Weighs Iran After the Vote
business_politics.latest_developments: Crude settled at two-month lows Wednesday, November 4, below $100 a barrel and down more than 8%, after Vice President JD Vance blamed the Republican midterm defeat on anger over the Iran war and traders bet the result pushes President Trump toward a settlement; gold futures recovered the $4,000 level, United States natural gas futures rose 2.2% to $2.959 per million British thermal units, and the Energy Information Administration reported a fifth straight weekly drop in commercial crude stocks, down 865,000 barrels, with distillate inventories at their lowest level in more than two decades. The Financial Times reported that two tankers changed course, stalling the White House gambit to buy Russian diesel and pull pump prices down, as American fuel supplies hit a 20-year low.
business_politics.summary: The war between the United States and Iran has set the price of oil and European gas since the summer, and Iran continues to use guerrilla tactics against tankers leaving the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, which keeps a risk premium in freight and fuel costs. Trump himself said the war cost Republicans votes, and the market now treats any sign of diplomacy with Tehran as the main lever on energy prices.

business_politics.title: CVS Splits in Two
business_politics.latest_developments: CVS Health confirmed Wednesday, November 4, that it will break up its healthcare empire, now valued at $102 billion, spinning off roughly 9,000 namesake drugstores, and it raised its full-year forecast the same morning on gains in health-care benefits and pharmacy.
business_politics.summary: CVS Health combines the Aetna insurer, the Caremark pharmacy benefit manager, and the retail pharmacy chain under one roof, and the separation arrives as Washington turns up political pressure on pharmacy benefit managers and health insurers. The company told investors it stays cautious on high medical costs even as it lifted guidance, and the breakup ranks among the largest restructurings the American healthcare industry has seen.

business_politics.title: Eurozone Inflation Reaches 4%
business_politics.latest_developments: Eurozone consumer prices rose 4% in the year to October, the fastest pace in three years and above forecasts, Sweden's Riksbank raised its key rate Wednesday, November 4, its first increase since the United States-Iran war began, and the WSJ Dollar Index closed down 0.30% at 96.94, its fifth loss in six sessions and a one-month low, which left the euro higher.
business_politics.summary: Core inflation across the single-currency bloc remains well above the European Central Bank's 2% target, which keeps the governing council on course for another tightening after it held the key rate at 2.5% on October 29, weeks before President Christine Lagarde leaves in February. The Riksbank signaled more increases ahead as war-driven energy costs work through European prices.

Heights Plaza, the shopping center in Harrison, sits mostly empty after a run of retailer departures.

business.latest_developments: The Chamber of Commerce Building, the 16-story redbrick office tower at 411 Seventh Avenue in downtown Pittsburgh, drew no outside bids at the Allegheny County sheriff's sale Monday, November 2, and went for $1.4 million, WPXI reported Wednesday, November 4.
business.summary: Builders put up the tower in 1900, and it occupies much of its downtown block. A sheriff's sale that attracts no outside bidder leaves the foreclosing lender holding the property, which puts the future of a full block of downtown office space in question.

business.latest_developments: The Jewish Community Foundation of the Jewish Federation of Greater Pittsburgh announced Monday, November 2, that it received a record $61.1 million in new contributions during fiscal year 2026, WPXI reported Wednesday, November 4.
business.summary: The foundation holds and invests endowment and donor-advised money for the Jewish Federation of Greater Pittsburgh, which funds social services, education, and community programs across the region. The record intake gives the federation a larger permanent base to spend from.

business.latest_developments: The Westmoreland County Industrial Development Authority takes up again Thursday, November 5, a request to issue up to $10 million in bond financing for a planned asphalt plant in East Huntingdon Township, TribLive reported Wednesday, November 4.
business.summary: The authority lends its tax-exempt borrowing capacity to private projects in Westmoreland County, and the asphalt plant's request has come before the board before. The decision determines whether the plant gets cheaper capital than a bank would supply.

business.title: Heating Grants Run $200 to $1,000
business.latest_developments: WPXI reported Wednesday, November 4, that eligible Peoples Natural Gas customers can collect grants of $200 to $1,000 toward winter heating bills from the state program that opened for applications Monday, November 2.
business.summary: Pennsylvania's Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program qualifies households by income and pays the money toward the heating bill, and Peoples Natural Gas, the gas utility across much of Western Pennsylvania, counts among the companies whose customers can apply. The grants land as gasoline and food prices dominate household budgets and the heating season starts.

business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Wednesday, November 4, that residents of Hempfield, the Westmoreland County township west of Greensburg, say water is seeping into their natural gas lines, a problem Ruth Shuga first noticed in 2023.
business.summary: Water inside a service line interrupts the gas flow that feeds furnaces, water heaters, and stoves, and the complaints surface in Hempfield as the heating season begins. Shuga and her neighbors have carried the issue for three years.

around_town.summary: Jefferson County, the north-central Pennsylvania county that takes in Brookville and Punxsutawney, has now recorded two of the six measles deaths the state has counted. around_town.title: Democrats Keep the Pennsylvania House
around_town.latest_developments: Democrats completed a Harrisburg trifecta for the first time in more than 30 years, holding the Pennsylvania House and taking a majority in the state Senate as Governor Josh Shapiro won a second term; Shapiro said Wednesday, November 4, that the Pennsylvania results give his party a blueprint elsewhere. Area results cut the other way in places: WPXI reported Wednesday evening that Representatives Mike Kelly and Guy Reschenthaler and state Representatives Aaron Bernstine, Josh Kail, and Roman Kozak all won reelection in southwestern Pennsylvania, while Republican Scott Timko beat Democratic Representative Brandon Dukes in House District 12, Republican Senator Camera Bartolotta turned back Independent Jodi Borello in Senate District 46, Democrat Hadley Haas unseated Republican Representative Valerie Gaydos in House District 44, Representative Rob Matzie held his seat, and Representatives Summer Lee of Swissvale and Chris Deluzio of Aspinwall won by more than 25 percentage points.
around_town.summary: The General Assembly writes Pennsylvania's budget, school funding formula, and election law, and both chambers were in play; the Butler County rematch in District 12 and the airport-area District 44 seat ranked among the handful of races that decided House control. Control of both chambers lets Shapiro move his priorities without negotiating with Republicans, and PublicSource notes it strengthens his hand should he run for president in 2028. The Pittsburgh region's congressional delegation stays as it was.

around_town.summary: Mars borough, the small town surrounded by fast-growing Adams Township along the Route 228 corridor north of Pittsburgh, shares services and school district boundaries with its neighbor. around_town.summary: The home rule charter amendment asked voters to loosen the limits on staffing for the 15-member Allegheny County Council, which sets the county budget and the property tax rate as County Executive Sara Innamorato weighs a reassessment. around_teams.title: Dulac Takes Trade Deadline Questions
around_teams.latest_developments: Gerry Dulac answered reader questions in his Post-Gazette Steelers chat Wednesday, November 4, with the conversation running through the NFL trade deadline that passed a day earlier.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh sits at 6-2 and leads the AFC North at the halfway point after the win over the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium, and the Post-Gazette had argued the day before the deadline that head coach Mike McCarthy's offense needs help at wide receiver.

sources.title: Gerry Dulac’s Steelers chat: 11.04.26
The Steelers need help at receiver. Which one should they target at the NFL trade deadline?

around_teams.title: The Pirates Shop the Free-Agent Market
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published a position-by-position survey Wednesday, November 4, of the free agents the Pirates could pursue this winter.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh opened its offseason by extending second baseman Brandon Lowe a qualifying offer worth $23.15 million, which Lowe has until November 17 to accept or reject, and the Post-Gazette has flagged a possible Major League Baseball lockout as the complication hanging over the club's shopping list.

sources.title: A position-by-position look at whom the Pirates could target in MLB free agency
The Pirates officially extend a qualifying offer to Brandon Lowe

around_teams.title: Mel Blount Sits Down With Heyward
around_teams.latest_developments: Not Just Football posted its conversation with Hall of Fame cornerback Mel Blount on Wednesday, November 4.
around_teams.summary: Blount told hosts Cam Heyward and Hayden Walsh how the Mel Blount Rule, the league's limit on hitting receivers downfield, grew out of the way he played, and he worked through Chuck Noll, the Steelers' 1974 draft class, the Immaculate Reception, the Steel Curtain, and the youth ranch he runs, closing with his read on the current NFL.

sources.source: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward
sources.title: Hall of Famer Mel Blount on Current NFL, Wild Steeler Stories, & His Rule | Not Just Football

around_teams.title: Benton and Heyward Grade Out as a Pair
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's Week 8 grades, published Wednesday, November 4, rate Keeanu Benton and Cam Heyward as a dynamic interior tandem for the Steelers.
around_teams.summary: Benton, the young nose tackle, lines up alongside Heyward, the defensive captain, on an interior front that the Post-Gazette credits with Pittsburgh's control of the line of scrimmage against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium. The grades extend the paper's argument that the defense has knit together around T.J. Watt at midseason.

sources.title: Steelers Week 8 grades: Keeanu Benton and Cam Heyward are becoming a dynamic DL duo

around_teams.title: Footbahlin Takes Stock at Midseason
around_teams.latest_developments: Ben Roethlisberger brought Charlie Batch onto Footbahlin's 145th episode, posted Tuesday, November 3, to sort out what the Steelers are at the halfway point after the Cleveland win.
around_teams.summary: Roethlisberger and his cohosts recorded from the bar while under the weather, and the episode works through the AFC North feel of the Browns game, the chirping and the collisions, and a defense they say finally plays to its paycheck. Batch, the former Steelers quarterback, helped them separate signal from noise on the 6-2 team.

sources.title: Win Over Browns and A Midseason Steelers Check-In w/Charlie Batch Ep 145

team_usa.title: John Nicks Dies at 97
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Wednesday, November 4, that John Nicks, the figure skating coach who tutored American Olympic champions Peggy Fleming and Kristi Yamaguchi, died Monday, November 2, at 97.
team_usa.summary: Nicks won a world pairs title skating for Britain with his sister before he built a coaching career in Southern California that produced United States and Olympic champions across six decades. Figure skating's Hall of Fame counts him a member, and United States skating officials called him an ambassador for the sport.

sources.title: John Nicks, 'tremendous ambassador' to sport of figure skating, dies at 97

team_usa.title: Pulisic, Balogun, and McKennie Return for Haiti
team_usa.latest_developments: The United States men's national team named its November squad Wednesday, November 4, for the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti, recalling AC Milan forward Christian Pulisic, AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun, and Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie.
team_usa.summary: Head coach Mauricio Pochettino blends those established starters with the teenagers who played well in the last window, a balancing act he carries into the Nations League knockout round and on toward the next World Cup cycle. Pulisic signed an AC Milan extension through 2031 last week, and Balogun returned to Monaco's European squad after scoring.

sources.title: Pulisic, Balogun, McKennie return to USMNT for Nations League QF vs. Haiti
Pochettino's squad illustrates his task: Blend prodigious prospects with USMNT's golden generation

team_usa.title: Rodman Starts Every Game for the Spirit
team_usa.latest_developments: Trinity Rodman told ESPN on Wednesday, November 4, that staying healthy enough to start every game this season gave her more satisfaction than the numbers, her most productive National Women's Soccer League regular season.
team_usa.summary: Rodman, the United States women's national team forward, plays for the Washington Spirit, which now chases the NWSL title; back trouble had limited her in previous seasons. Her teammate Hal Hershfelt tore an ACL in late October and will miss the rest of the Spirit's run.

sources.title: Trinity Rodman 'really blessed' for healthy season after past injuries
